findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet rather than keeping it private within the VPC.
storage_encrypted = false means the RDS volume and its snapshots are unencrypted, so database contents are readable by anyone who obtains the underlying storage or a snapshot.
The master password is supplied through var.password and hard-passed to the instance; combined with the default 'admin' username this places a plaintext credential in Terraform state and plan output.
No parameter/option enforces SSL for MySQL connections (require_secure_transport is not set in the parameter group), so client traffic to the publicly reachable database can be unencrypted.
The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", so compromise of the EC2 web server yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2 infrastructure, and RDS databases in the account.

The database master password and username are interpolated into EC2 user_data, which is stored unencrypted and retrievable by any process or attacker able to reach the instance metadata service (169.254.169.254/latest/user-data).

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled and SSRF against the PHP application could be used to steal the over-privileged instance role credentials and the user-data secrets.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root volume (which holds the dbinfo.inc file containing the DB password) may be stored unencrypted.

The instance is deployed into a subnet and exposes a public DNS name (surfaced as an output) while serving an HTTP-only PHP application that accepts POST input, creating internet-facing attack surface with no TLS.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting data exfiltration or C2 callbacks from a compromised database host.

The DB security group allows port 3306 from the entire VPC CIDR rather than just the application security group, and because the instance is publicly_accessible this group is the only control preventing internet reachability.
The database endpoint of a publicly accessible instance is exported as a non-sensitive output, making the attack target easy to discover from state or CI logs.
